prize_parts.citation: for the invention and experimental development of optical lattice clocks

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed from B011 to B031. WMAP remains an extraordinary, mature observational transformation, but the round-1 exchange makes clearer that optical lattice clocks meet the same demanding test of demonstrated physical consequence while offering a more compact and presently more defensible allocation of credit. Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's decisive experimental development created a reproducible regime in which neutral-atom spectroscopy became an exceptionally precise probe of time, gravitation, and fundamental physics. The case rests on capabilities already demonstrated across independent laboratories, not on a prospective redefinition of the second or unspecified future applications.
statement.case_against: B031 is still vulnerable if described merely as an accumulation of metrological improvements rather than a distinct atomic-physics breakthrough. Historical review must delimit the foundational lattice-clock advance from later international gains in performance and determine whether Katori and Ye alone represent the indispensable conceptual and experimental contributions. WMAP has the stronger claim to a settled cosmological transformation, so the switch reflects attributional clarity and the demonstrated new measurement regime, not any downgrading of its scientific importance.

responses.point: Kroll argues that independently reproduced lattice clocks already enable precision measurements of gravitation and fundamental physics, without relying on a future standards decision.
responses.response: I find this resolves my principal maturity reservation. A possible redefinition of the second is irrelevant to the award: the prize-worthy result is the experimentally established ability to interrogate many neutral atoms in a controlled magic-wavelength lattice and thereby make new precision measurements. This is evidence from nature, not simply an elegant metrological prospect.

responses.point: Lindroth emphasizes that the magic-wavelength lattice changes the physical possibility of high-precision neutral-atom interrogation and that Katori and Ye offer a focused conceptual and experimental attribution.
responses.response: I agree with this framing. It distinguishes the achievement from routine optimization of a clock. The proposed citation should remain narrow—about invention and experimental development of optical lattice clocks—so that it neither claims all later clock advances nor turns a standards-policy outcome into the discovery.

responses.point: Pearce regards high-energy neutrino astronomy as profound but judges its sparse source identifications and large-collaboration attribution less secure than the lattice-clock case.
responses.response: I retain B044 as an important alternative because a new cosmic messenger is an exceptionally compelling achievement. Yet the distinction Pearce draws is decisive here: B031 has both a mature, broadly reproducible physical capability and an unusually coherent two-person attribution, whereas the appropriate individual allocation for IceCube remains harder to establish.

uncertainties: Whether the historical record supports limiting the central optical-lattice-clock achievement to Katori and Ye rather than adding another indispensable experimental pioneer.
Whether the citation can preserve the discrete magic-wavelength atomic-physics breakthrough while excluding subsequent worldwide performance improvements and applications.
Whether Bennett, Spergel, and Page adequately represent the experimental, analytical, and collaboration-wide contributions to WMAP if B011 is reconsidered.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
